_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 4.2. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Which body openings are covered by the offence of rape under s. 1 SOA 2003?
A woman holds down the victim while her male friend rapes him. What is her liability?
options: She is guilty of rape as an accessory
explanations: She can't be the principal, but can be an accessory.

questions.scenario: B consents to intercourse but after a minute tells A to stop. A continues. Which statement is correct?
options: No offence – consent was given at the start
Rape – penetration is a continuing act and consent was withdrawn

questions.scenario: How does s. 74 SOA 2003 define consent?
options: Agreeing by choice, having the freedom and capacity to make that choice
explanations: Must be free and with capacity.

questions.scenario: Which of these is an EVIDENTIAL (rebuttable) presumption under s. 75?
options: A deceived B about the nature of the act
B was asleep at the time and A knew this

questions.scenario: What is the effect of a s. 75 presumption once the circumstance is proved and A knew of it?
options: B is presumed not to have consented and A not to have reasonably believed it, unless sufficient evidence is adduced to raise an issue
The burden is on A to prove consent beyond reasonable doubt
explanations: A must only raise an issue.

questions.scenario: Which of these is a CONCLUSIVE presumption under s. 76?
options: Violence was used immediately before the act
A drug was given to B without consent
A intentionally deceived B as to the nature or purpose of the act

questions.scenario: A pretends to be B's long-term partner in a dark bedroom; B consents believing it is her partner. Which is correct?
options: Conclusive presumption under s. 76 – impersonation of a person known personally to B

questions.scenario: A singing teacher tells a pupil that intercourse will improve her voice; she agrees. Which statement fits best?
options: Deception as to the purpose of the act – s. 76 conclusive presumption

questions.scenario: A lies to B that he is rich and single to persuade her to have sex. Under R v Jheeta, how is this analysed?
options: Not under s. 76 – it isn't about nature or purpose; consider s. 74

questions.scenario: Under s. 75, a stupefying substance was given to B without her consent. Who must have administered it?
options: Anyone – the presumption applies whoever administered it, if A knew

questions.scenario: How is the reasonableness of A's belief in consent determined?
options: Having regard to all the circumstances, including any steps A took to ascertain whether B consented

questions.scenario: A is very drunk and says he genuinely believed B consented. Does his intoxication help?
options: Yes – it makes the belief reasonable
No – voluntary intoxication cannot make an unreasonable belief reasonable
Only if B was also drunk

questions.scenario: B is drunk but still has capacity and agrees to sex. Following R v Bree, which is correct?
options: A drunken consent is still consent if B retains capacity
No consent is possible when drunk
explanations: Intoxication isn't a s. 75 circumstance unless a substance was administered without consent.

questions.scenario: Does 'vagina' in the SOA 2003 include the vulva?
A transgender woman has a surgically constructed vagina. Can she be a victim of rape by penetration of it?
options: Yes – references to body parts include surgically constructed parts (s. 79(3))
Only if recognised by a GRC

questions.scenario: A man, 19, has intercourse with a 12-year-old girl who said she was 16 and agreed. Which offence?
options: Rape of a child under 13 (s. 5) – consent and belief as to age irrelevant
Sexual activity with a child (s. 9) only

questions.scenario: Following R v G (2008), liability as to the age of the child under s. 5 is…
What is the maximum penalty for rape?
Mode of trial for rape?
B is threatened that her brother outside will be beaten immediately unless she submits. Which applies?
options: Nothing – threat was to someone else
s. 75 evidential presumption – fear that immediate violence would be used against another person

questions.scenario: B, who is paralysed and cannot speak, is unable to communicate whether she consents. Which applies?
options: s. 75 – physical disability preventing communication of consent

questions.scenario: For a s. 75 presumption to apply, what must the prosecution prove about A's state of mind?
options: That A knew the relevant circumstance existed

questions.scenario: A threatens B with the loss of her job unless she has sex. B submits. Which is correct?
options: Not a s. 75/76 case; the jury decide under s. 74 whether B agreed by choice with freedom
explanations: It may be rape under s. 74.

questions.scenario: Which of the following best describes submission?
options: Not necessarily consent – a person may submit without agreeing by choice

questions.scenario: A puts his penis in B's mouth without consent. Which offence?
explanations: It is penile penetration by A – rape.

questions.scenario: Where B was unlawfully detained at the time, when does the s. 75 presumption NOT apply?
options: When A was also unlawfully detained
explanations: Correct – it requires that A was not detained.

questions.scenario: In an exam question, how much penetration is required for rape?
options: Penetration for at least a minute

questions.scenario: A says he thought B consented because she didn't say no while she lay still. What does the court consider?
options: Only that she didn't say no
All the circumstances, including what steps A took to find out whether she consented

questions.scenario: Which statement about s. 76 is correct?
options: It cannot be rebutted once the facts are proved
It can be rebutted by evidence
